status: Recorded 12 October 2026 before step 6 measurements. Values were entered from the author's knowledge of the cited grammars and the World Atlas of Language Structures (WALS) feature definitions; they were not re-checked online in this run. Each row should be verified against the cited source before reuse.

features.nominal_affixes: Whether case and number marking on nouns is predominantly suffixal or prefixal (cf. WALS 26A, which covers all inflection).
features.genitive_noun: Order of possessor (genitive) and possessed noun (WALS 86A).
features.numeral_noun: Order of cardinal numeral and counted noun in speech (WALS 89A). Administrative writing can differ: Ur III accounts write the numeral before the commodity although Sumerian speech places it after the noun.

candidates.name: Proto-Dravidian (from Old Tamil and the comparative record)
sources: Krishnamurti, B. 2003. The Dravidian Languages. Cambridge University Press, chapters 6 and 7
Steever, S. B. (ed.) 1998. The Dravidian Languages. Routledge

candidates.name: Old Indo-Aryan (Vedic Sanskrit)
candidates.nominal_affixes: suffixing (verbal preverbs and augment are prefixal)
sources: Macdonell, A. A. 1916. A Vedic Grammar for Students. Oxford
Whitney, W. D. 1889. Sanskrit Grammar. 2nd ed.

candidates.name: Munda (Santali, Mundari; Proto-Munda reconstructions)
candidates.nominal_affixes: suffixing case marking; prefixes and infixes in derivation; reconstructed Proto-Munda and Witzel's Para-Munda substrate retain prefixes
sources: Anderson, G. D. S. (ed.) 2008. The Munda Languages. Routledge
Witzel, M. 1999. Substrate languages in Old Indo-Aryan. Electronic Journal of Vedic Studies 5(1)

candidates.name: Burushaski
candidates.nominal_affixes: suffixing on nouns; pronominal prefixes on some nouns and verbs
sources: Berger, H. 1998. Die Burushaski-Sprache von Hunza und Nager. Harrassowitz

candidates.name: Elamite
sources: Stolper, M. W. 2004. Elamite. In R. D. Woodard (ed.), The Cambridge Encyclopedia of the World's Ancient Languages

candidates.name: Sumerian
candidates.nominal_affixes: suffixing (case enclitics at the end of the noun phrase; verbal prefix chain)
candidates.numeral_noun: N-Num in speech; Num-N in administrative writing
sources: Jagersma, A. H. 2010. A Descriptive Grammar of Sumerian. PhD thesis, Leiden
Thomsen, M.-L. 1984. The Sumerian Language. Copenhagen

candidates.name: Akkadian
candidates.nominal_affixes: suffixing case endings; verbal person prefixes
sources: Huehnergard, J. 2011. A Grammar of Akkadian. 3rd ed. Eisenbrauns

observable_mapping.assumption: Seal texts are noun phrases (names, titles, possessors) written with at least partly logographic units in reading order.
observable_mapping.head_final_prediction: Gen-N and Adj-N languages place modifiers before the head; a recurring head noun or case marker closes the text, so a small set of signs concentrates at text ends and the most variable material comes first.
observable_mapping.head_initial_prediction: N-Gen and N-Adj languages place the head first; recurring relational nouns (son, servant) and titles occur early or medially, before the name they govern.
observable_mapping.affix_prediction: Suffixing nominal morphology concentrates a small set of recurring signs at the ends of units; prefixing concentrates them at the starts.
observable_mapping.limit: Determinatives written at word ends (as in Egyptian) produce the same final concentration as suffixes, so the affix statistic cannot separate grammar from writing convention.
